title: Coordination-controlled photophysics and antiproliferative activity of coumarin-linked schiff bases and Zn(II) complexes.
authors: Pham, Thanh Chung; Pham, Van Thong; Tran, Ngoc Dung; Nandanwar, Sondavid; Nguyen, Van Trang; Nguyen, Trung Huy; Nguyen, Xuyen Thi; Cao, Hong Thi; Vo, Anh Kieu Thi; Pham, Duong Quang; Nguyen, Tuan Anh; Nam, Pham Thi; Tran, Dai Lam; Lee, Songyi
journal: Photochemical & photobiological sciences : Official journal of the European Photochemistry Association and the European Society for Photobiology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究香豆素席夫碱及Zn(II)配合物的光物理与抗癌活性，虽含DNA结合实验和分子对接/MD模拟，但核心对象为小分子-蛋白/DNA，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA体系，方法可迁移性有限。
abstract: In this work, two coumarin-linked Schiff bases, Cou-NEt and Cou-Nap, together with their Zn(II)-derived products, were synthesized and investigated by spectroscopic, computational, and biological methods. Structural characterization revealed distinct Zn(II)-dependent outcomes: Cou-Nap afforded the expected Zn(II) complex, whereas reaction of Cou-NEt with ZnCl(2) induced imine cleavage to yield an amine-derived Zn(II) species. All compounds showed similar visible absorption bands, while Zn(II) incorporation modified the emission response and enhanced fluorescence, most prominently for Zn-Nap. TD-DFT calculations indicated predominantly ligand-centered excited states and suggested that the weak fluorescence of Cou-NEt is associated with access to a red-shifted keto-like excited state, whereas Zn(II) coordination suppresses nonradiative deactivation through chelation-induced rigidification. DNA-binding experiments revealed moderate affinity toward ctDNA, consistent with non-covalent interaction. In vitro antiproliferative assays against MCF-7, HepG2, and A549 cells showed that Cou-NEt and Zn-Nap were the most active compounds in the present series. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations using the human mTORDeltaN-mLST8 complex supported favorable binding profiles for these two compounds, while confocal imaging in HeLa cells demonstrated efficient cellular uptake of the Zn(II) species. Overall, the results show that Zn(II) coordination can tune the photophysical and anticancer-related behavior of coumarin-based Schiff-base systems in a ligand-dependent manner, while further structural optimization is required to improve antiproliferative potency.
abstract_zh: 本工作中，合成了两种香豆素连接的席夫碱Cou-NEt和Cou-Nap及其Zn(II)衍生产物，并通过光谱学、计算和生物学方法进行了研究。结构表征揭示了不同的Zn(II)依赖性结果：Cou-Nap生成了预期的Zn(II)配合物，而Cou-NEt与ZnCl(2)的反应诱导亚胺裂解，产生了一种胺衍生的Zn(II)物种。所有化合物表现出相似的可见吸收带，而Zn(II)的引入改变了发射响应并增强了荧光，其中Zn-Nap最为显著。TD-DFT计算表明，激发态主要为配体中心性质，并提示Cou-NEt的弱荧光与进入红移的酮类激发态有关，而Zn(II)配位通过螯合诱导的刚性化抑制了非辐射失活。DNA结合实验显示对ctDNA具有中等亲和力，与非共价相互作用一致。针对MCF-7、HepG2和A549细胞的体外抗增殖实验表明，Cou-NEt和Zn-Nap在本系列中活性最高。使用人mTORDeltaN-mLST8复合物的分子对接和分子动力学模拟支持了这两种化合物的有利结合特性，而HeLa细胞中的共聚焦成像证明了Zn(II)物种的高效细胞摄取。总体而言，结果表明Zn(II)配位能以配体依赖性方式调节香豆素基席夫碱体系的光物理和抗癌相关行为，同时需要进一步的结构优化以提高抗增殖效力。
